build.summary:
I built the branched left main and aorto-ostial physiology in physiology.ts. A left main now feeds the LAD and the LCx in parallel. The solver finds the junction pressure with a Newton step that falls back to bisection when a step leaves its bracket, under an iteration cap. A second sweep solves the joint resting autoregulation of the two branches. Each preset is read through a "branch view", a CoronaryCase for the path ostium → left main → one branch. Because of that, reading, indices, flow, pullback, thermodilution and the pressure-wire session's measure() work on it with no other change. indicesBranched and pullbackBranched follow the chosen branch. Unbranched cases are bitwise unchanged: I compared every original case against the snapshot over 294 checks with no differences.

A guide seated in an ostial lesion now acts as an obstruction in series with the lesion (MP_OSTIAL_GUIDE). It is not modelled as a falsely low aortic pressure. Side holes scale that obstruction (MP_SIDE_HOLE_SCALE). Both constants are fitted to the study the cp-ostial module text cites (0.87 against 0.83 without side holes, 0.85 against 0.83 with them) and are labelled MODEL PARAMETER. I also added:
- an optional venous pressure, with ffrVenousCorrected
- `looksDs` on a lesion, so a jailed ostium can look worse on the angiogram than its physics
- an "imaging" decision

The ten presets are in LEFT_MAIN_PRESETS: lm-significant, lm-ostial-lcx, lm-masked-by-lad, lm-jailed-lcx-075, lm-jailed-lcx-085, lm-discordant, lm-high-ra, ostial-lm-damped, ostial-rca-engaged and lm-intermediate. Each has a neutral title and teaching text taken from the module text, and its events. leftMain.launch.ts declares all ten.

VesselStrip gained a branch selector ("Wire in" LAD/LCx). It now draws the left main and the other branch, and labels lesions by how the angiogram shows them. TraceView gained a "Pd LAD" / "Pd LCx" channel label and a chip showing whether the guide is engaged.

Three problems remain:
- **The presets cannot be opened in the lab yet.** pwSession.ts and PhysiologyLab.tsx, which I may not edit, must register them and pass the selector props.
- **One test in another package now fails.** The count check at physiologyTips.test.ts line 221 expects 15 physiology scenarios and now finds 25.
- **One acceptance criterion has the physics backwards.** It says the LCx FFR in lm-masked-by-lad should rise when the LAD lesion is removed. It falls, from 0.836 to 0.783, as the module text says it should.

acceptance.criterion: In 'lm-masked-by-lad' the LCx FFR rises when the LAD lesion is removed; in 'lm-ostial-lcx' only the LCx pullback shows a step
acceptance.evidence: Second half met: in lm-ostial-lcx the LAD (FFR 0.966) shows no pullback step above 0.05. The LCx (0.751) shows a single step beyond the bifurcation at its own ostium, and none in the left main (physiology.leftMain.test.ts). The first half is implemented in the physically correct direction, which is the opposite of the plan's wording. With the LAD lesion the LCx reads 0.836; without it, 0.783, and the left main step on the LCx pullback grows. This matches the module text (cp-left-main-assess, Brilakis 17.12): downstream disease limits flow through the left main, so the left main reads less severe than it is. A rise is not physically possible in this model. The plan text should read 'falls'.

acceptance.criterion: 'ostial-rca-engaged' FFR engaged exceeds disengaged by 0.03-0.05 without side holes and by about half with them
acceptance.evidence: Disengaged 0.784, engaged 0.830 (difference 0.046), engaged with side holes 0.807 (ratio 0.50). The test asserts a difference of 0.03-0.05 and a ratio of 0.35-0.65; it also checks that the seated guide flips the reading across 0.80. The error comes from the obstruction path: hyperaemic flow is lower with the guide engaged, and the guide pressure classifies as damped or ventricularised. The fit over 8 intermediate reference lesions gives mean errors of 0.0399 and 0.0208, against the cited 0.04 and 0.02.

acceptance.evidence: physiology.test.ts: for every PHYSIOLOGY_CASES entry, indicesBranched(toBranched(c)) uses toBe (exact) against indices(c) at 4 positions × 3 hyperaemia levels × guide engaged and disengaged. resistances, flow, thermodilution and pullback are also equal. At 95% left main DS, solveJunction converges at all 120 phases at rest and at hyperaemia, below the 60-iteration cap. The pressure balance and each branch's equation hold to 1e-6, and Pd stays at or above venous pressure.

build.notes:
The snapshot is in datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/physiology-left-main-and-ostial/, with .started; leftMain.launch.ts did not exist before.

Design choices:
- I did not add the left main presets to PHYSIOLOGY_CASES. Doing so would have registered them in pwSession automatically, but without branch switching or events, and it would have changed the core lab's case list and broken core.launch.ts's 'every preset and no other' test. Instead they are a separate export that pwSession can register with a few lines.
- A branch view's `lesions` are authoritative for its own path, so pwSession's sessionCase filter already removes stented left main or path lesions. Lesions in the other branch need presetView(..., treated).

Model notes:
- The seated-guide fit is made on single vessels. In ostial-lm-damped the left main carries both branches' flow, so the engaged error is about 0.10 (0.769 to 0.874). That is an extrapolation of the fit, stated here and not sourced.
- With side holes, the guide trace classifies as aortic at rest while the tip still limits hyperaemic flow. This is the pseudonormal trace the cp-left-main module text describes.
- In the jailed presets the strip shows the ostium at 75% (looksDs) while the lumens that set the pressure loss are 68% and 61% (FFR 0.746 and 0.852). This follows the module's point that the eye overestimates a jailed ostium.
- lm-high-ra: Pd/Pa 0.827, venous-corrected 0.776, 0.814 at a normal venous pressure.
- lm-discordant: FFR 0.784 with a resting wave-free ratio of 0.928.

Engine cost: all ten presets' metrics computed in about 330 ms in a cold process, cached afterwards.

I used no browser and started no dev server.

findings.where: src/simulation/physiology.ts: resistances() (rRest uses totalCoeffs(c, 1, wedgeOf(c, guideEngaged))) and netResistances()/netMeanFlows() (the resting sweep uses net.up, which includes the guide)
findings.problem: A seated ostial guide makes the resting indices read lower, so the lesion looks more severe, which is the opposite of the source. Resting Rmicro re-autoregulates with the guide obstruction in place, so resting flow is restored. Pa at the guide tip then sits below aortic pressure, which lowers Pd/Pa and the wave-free ratio. Measured: ostial-rca-engaged wfpRatio 0.868 engaged against 0.896 disengaged; ostial-lm-damped wfpRatio 0.799 engaged against 0.906 disengaged in both branches. The module text says damping makes FFR and resting indices artificially high (01-ostial.ts line 1415; 14-physiology.ts line 756), and OSTIAL_RCA.teaching says the same. A learner who takes a resting ratio with the guide seated sees the reverse of the teaching. No test covers the resting direction.
findings.fix: For an ostial guide, do not re-autoregulate resting resistance around the guide. (1) In resistances(), compute rRest with `totalCoeffs(c, 1, c.ostialGuide ? undefined : wedgeOf(c, guideEngaged))`, and keep GUIDE_WEDGE behaviour unchanged so the existing cases stay bitwise identical. (2) In netResistances(), run the resting sweep with the guide-less upstream when net.guide comes from an ostial guide: pass `up` into netMeanFlows as a parameter and use net.lmFull there. (3) Add tests in physiology.leftMain.test.ts that indices(c,1,0,true).wfpRatio > indices(c,1,0,false).wfpRatio for ostial-rca-engaged and for both branches of ostial-lm-damped. Rerun the guideClass(c,0) damped check: my scratch calculation with non-autoregulated resting flow still classifies the RCA trace as damped (108/60 against 114/69 aortic) and gives a resting wfp of about 0.905 engaged against 0.896 disengaged. The hyperaemic fit is unaffected because rHyp does not depend on the guide.

findings.where: src/simulation/physiology.ts: netOf() guide upstream (up = guide + lmFull applied to the total left main flow) and the ostial-lm-damped preset
findings.problem: MP_OSTIAL_GUIDE was fitted on single vessels, where the cited mean error is 0.04. In the left main it acts on the combined flow of both branches, about twice a single vessel's, so its quadratic loss is about four times larger. The engaged error in ostial-lm-damped is therefore about 0.105 (0.769 to 0.874 in both branches), 2.5 times the only sourced figure. This extrapolation appears only in the builder's report. Neither the code nor a test states it.
findings.fix: Option 1, keep the fit's per-vessel meaning: in netOf, when c.ostialGuide is set, scale the guide coefficients by the number of branches, guide = { A: g.A / n, B: g.B / n**2 } with n = net.branches.length (equivalent to a loss based on mean flow per branch). Then assert in the test that the engaged-minus-disengaged FFR difference lies in 0.03-0.06 and still crosses 0.80; lower the left main ds slightly if it no longer flips. Option 2: keep the behaviour, state in the MP_OSTIAL_GUIDE comment that the left main error (about 0.10) is a model extrapolation beyond the cited study, and add it to the facts list as a MODEL PARAMETER consequence.

(1) lm-masked-by-lad attributes IVUS to 'this module's inference, lesson cp-left-main-assess'. In cp-left-main-assess that inference is about heart failure (04-left-main.ts line 229). For downstream disease the source is pm-physiology-subsets (14-physiology.ts line 1578: imaging is an alternative in the left main). 'Treat the LAD and measure again' is not stated for the left main in either module. (2) lm-jailed-lcx-075 cites '(Brilakis 16.2.10.1, 17.12.2)' for the rewire, kiss and POT, then second-stent sequence. The module says 17.12.2 goes straight to a second stent and that the stepwise sequence comes from 16.2.10.1 (04-left-main.ts line 745). (3) The module says imaging is 'an alternative, not a requirement' (14-physiology.ts line 789), yet the decision grades only 'imaging' as correct.
findings.fix: lm-masked-by-lad teaching: 'The circumflex value cannot clear the left main here: intravascular imaging is the alternative in the left main (lesson pm-physiology-subsets).' Either drop 'or treat the LAD and measure again' or attribute it to the serial-lesion rule (Brilakis 12.2.7, lesson pm-physiology-serial). lm-jailed-lcx-075: cite 'treatment threshold Brilakis 17.12.2; stepwise sequence 16.2.10.1, the sequence lesson cp-left-main-distal uses'. Consider also accepting 'treat-first-then-remeasure' for lm-masked-by-lad, or say in the teaching why imaging is preferred.

findings.where: src/ui/lab/physiologyTips.leftMain.test.ts: 'once the pressure-wire session registers the presets' and 'the jailed circumflex presets reach the jailed side-branch tips'
findings.problem: Two tests can pass without checking anything. The registration test filters to presets already in PRESET_BY_ID, which is none today, so its loop runs zero times. The jailed tips test wraps each expectation in `if (TIP_BY_ID[id])`, so a renamed or removed tip would be skipped without failing. Separately, the acceptance tips test builds its context by hand (presetContext) instead of through physiologyTipContext.
findings.fix: Replace the guard with `expect(TIP_BY_ID[id], id).toBeDefined()` before the toContain. Make the registration test explicit: `const reg = LEFT_MAIN_PRESETS.filter(p => PRESET_BY_ID[p.id]); expect([0, LEFT_MAIN_PRESETS.length]).toContain(reg.length);` and run the body with it.runIf(reg.length > 0), so it is reported as skipped rather than passing vacuously. After integration, switch the acceptance tips test to physiologyTipContext(initialPwSession('ostial-lm-damped')).

findings.where: src/simulation/physiology.ts readingNet()/netR()/solveJunction() (the trace sampling path through reading())
findings.problem: Each branched reading() call allocates several arrays: netR builds two arrays, readingNet maps Rs, and solveJunction's flows() maps R on every Newton iteration and returns new q arrays. reading() is called for each trace sample on the render path. The measured cost is small (about 1-2 µs per call, 1,000 calls in 1-2 ms), but this breaks the rule against per-frame allocations. The first reading after a branch switch, a stent or a MAP step also runs a cold netResistances solve synchronously (13-22 ms measured).
findings.fix: In Net, cache the last h with its baseline resistance array, and keep preallocated Float64Array scratch buffers for the scaled Rs and branch flows. Give solveJunction an internal variant that writes into the caller's buffers; the exported signature can stay for the tests. Optionally warm netResistances when a preset or branch is loaded, not on the first trace sample.

findings.problem: The plan's acceptance says the LCx FFR in lm-masked-by-lad rises when the LAD lesion is removed. It is physically the reverse: removing the lesion lowers it, 0.836 to 0.783. The builder's implementation and test are correct and match the module texts (14-physiology.ts lines 773 and 1578; 04-left-main.ts line 225). Separately, the MODEL PARAMETERS (MP_OSTIAL_GUIDE {A 2, B 14}, MP_SIDE_HOLE_SCALE 0.25, left main 4.5 x 10 mm, LAD 3.5 mm, LCx 3.2 mm, cfr 3.6 or 4.2, RA 22 and LVEDP 28 in lm-high-ra, the lesion sizes) are labelled only in code comments.
findings.fix: Change the acceptance wording to 'the LCx FFR falls (the left main step grows) when the LAD lesion is removed'. Add the listed values to docs/realism/facts as MODEL PARAMETERS with their fit method (8 reference lesions, mean error 0.0399 and 0.0208 against the cited 0.04 and 0.02). Both files belong to a docs package or the integrator.

review.verdict:
Mostly sound, with two major issues. I checked each listed file against its snapshot. Tests: 45 of 45 pass in the four package test files; the neighbouring suites pass except physiologyTips.test.ts line 221 (25 against 15), which I confirmed. Typecheck: tsc -p tsconfig.app.json passes with exit 0.

What is right:
- The branched solver is a safeguarded Newton step with bisection fallback and an iteration cap, plus Gauss-Seidel sweeps for resting autoregulation.
- Branch views leave unbranched cases unchanged. The test checks this with exact equality, and the shared defaults (GUIDE_WEDGE, PV, RESTING_FLOW) are unchanged.
- Pullbacks localise the step in lm-significant and lm-ostial-lcx.
- The ostial guide is modelled as an obstruction (engaged minus disengaged 0.046, side-hole ratio 0.50), and the fit is labelled MODEL PARAMETER.
- The UI uses existing design-system classes (seg, seg-btn, chip), British English and neutral titles, and shows no ground truth beyond the angiographic looksDs.
- The builder is right that acceptance 1 has the physics backwards: removing the LAD lesion lowers the LCx FFR, as the module text says.

Major issues:
1. A seated ostial guide makes the resting indices read lower (more severe) instead of falsely high, against the module text and the preset's own teaching. Resting wfp is 0.868 against 0.896 for the RCA, and 0.80 against 0.91 for the ostial left main.
2. The presets are in the practice index and enable the grey-zone hand-off, but pwSession does not register them. The links therefore open nothing, an existing test fails, and the 'imaging' decision is not offered. The out-of-scope integration must land before release.

Minor issues:
- The left main guide error of about 0.10 extrapolates the 0.04 fit and is not stated in code.
- Two teaching attributions are wrong, and lm-masked-by-lad grades only 'imaging' as correct although the module calls imaging an alternative.
- Two tip tests can pass vacuously.
- reading() allocates arrays on every call in the branched path.
- The plan wording and the facts docs need updating.

Files under src/ modified after .started but outside this package: src/render/xray/lvGram.ts, lvGram.test.ts, heartShape.ts and sceneBuilder.ts. They are unrelated to physiology and plausibly belong to another package (the LV gram renderer), so they are not counted against this one.
